sections.html:
• Also known as Echinodorus angustifolia, Echinodorus 'Vesuvius' and Helanthium 'Vesuvius'.
  • Narrow-leafed sword plant whose blades grow in a spiral.
  • Height: approximately 10 to 12 inches (about 25 to 30 cm).
  • Light: takes low to high light, prefers at least medium.
  • CO2 is not necessary but helps faster growth.
  • Heavy root feeder; spreads by runners.

Vesuvius is usually grown above water (emersed) at plant farms, so you may receive a plant with wider leaves and even flower buds. These emersed-grown leaves will melt back after planting in your aquarium, and new submersed-grown leaves in their slender form will soon appear.

Growing to approximately 10 to 12 inches (25 to 30 cm) tall, it can be used as a midground plant for medium to large tanks or as a background plant for nano tanks. With medium light, neutral pH and root tab fertilizers it will readily grow and spread to create a lush jungle look. It can take low to high lighting but prefers at least medium light. Carbon dioxide (CO2) injection is not necessary but will help with faster growth.

As with most sword plants, vesuvius is a heavy root feeder that does best with a nutrient-rich substrate or root tab fertilizers. Once it establishes a good root system and is growing well, it readily reproduces by sending out runners (much like vallisneria and dwarf sagittaria), creating a gnarled forest in your aquarium.

Similar to corkscrew vallisneria, vesuvius looks like curly underwater grass, but its blades are narrower and grow in a tighter twist. Its common name was chosen because the leaves appear to be rising from the base of the plant much like the smoke wisps spiraling out of Mount Vesuvius. This unusual plant is still relatively new to the aquarium hobby, but it is easy to grow and adds interesting texture to a planted tank.

Aquascapers often seek to add variety with attention-grabbing specimens such as red plants, carpeting plants and unique textures. Vesuvius fits well in the latter category.
